 For the past year, the Detroit Tigers and contract negotiations with star pitchers have gone hand in hand. Tarik Skubal and the Tigers couldn't come to terms on an extension, so they wound up trading him to help with the future of the franchise.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But one offseason after failing to extend Skubal, the Tigers have managed to work out a contract extension with a key young breakout pitcher.
 According to ESPN's Jeff Passan , the Tigers are signing Troy Melton to a huge six-year, $46.5 million contract extension to keep him in Detroit through the 2033 season.
 Tigers agree to $46.5M extension with Troy Melton
 "BREAKING: Right-hander Troy Melton and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension, sources tell ESPN," Passan reports. "Deal includes a club option for 2033 and can max out at $80 million. Big payday for the 25-year-old with 160 career major league innings."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Tigers, after losing Skubal after being unable to sign him to a contract extension, have avoided making the same mistake with Melton.
 After posting a 2.76 ERA in 20 starts for the Tigers this past season, Melton has agreed to a massive pay raise to stay with the Tigers for the next six-plus seasons.
 Detroit can now keep Melton through the 2033 MLB season if all goes well with this new deal, which, if his first 36 MLB appearances are any indication, should come to fruition.
 MORE : Dodgers, Blue Jays, Mets, Padres reportedly in bidding war for $32M two-time Cy Young winner 
 Over the last two seasons, Melton has appeared in 36 games, posting a 2.76 ERA with 11 wins and seven losses and 130 strikeouts across 160 innings of work.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Tigers have likely seen enough and believe the 25-year-old should be a key part of the future in Detroit. Melton, the young breakout right-hander, is getting a big payday that can potentially reach upwards of $80 million total.
 This decision from the Tigers is a very smart one, as the promise Melton has shown so far is worth investing in. Now, they have locked Melton up for an extra couple of seasons and handed him a nice raise to do it.
